title: Ink coverage
description:
Reports how much of the host PICTURE is ink, and outlines its extent.

The smallest possible image-hosted object, and its job is to prove the host works: attach it to an imported drawing and the Metrics tab should show a coverage figure that changes when you move the threshold, with a rectangle drawn around the picture at its true size in metres.

WHAT IT READS. `img` is the host — the downsampled luminance matrix, 0..1, low = ink — bound by the image host exactly as the flow's Image node publishes it on `val-matrix`. Beside it arrive `originX`, `originY`, `cellM`, `widthM` and `heightM`, the same placement readings, in anchor-relative metres. A body written against a Vectorise-style flow reads those names unchanged, which is the point: maths ported from the flow editor works here without being rewritten.

THRESHOLD is the one dial. A cell counts as ink when it is darker than this. 0.5 suits a clean line drawing; lower it for a pale scan, raise it for a drawing on a grey ground. Coverage is the count of inked cells over the total, so it is a proportion of the PICTURE, not of the plan.

THE MATRIX IS DOWNSAMPLED — at most 128 cells on its long edge, the same limit the flow's Image node uses. `Cell size` reports how wide one cell is in metres. Coverage is therefore a fair estimate rather than a pixel count, and a hairline thinner than a cell may not register at all.

LIMITS. It reads LUMINANCE only, so a coloured line and a black one of the same darkness count alike, and anything pale — hatching, a watermark, a light grey fill — is invisible below the threshold. It is a sanity check on the picture, not a measurement of the drawing.

params.name: Count the ink
params.expr:
# INK COVERAGE OF THE HOST PICTURE.
# `img` is the host: the downsampled 0..1 LUMINANCE matrix, LOW = ink, bound by the image host exactly
# as the flow's Image node publishes it on `val-matrix`. `originX` / `originY` / `cellM` / `widthM` /
# `heightM` arrive beside it and say where those cells sit, in anchor-relative metres.

# A cell counts as INK when it is darker than the threshold. `le` gives a 0/1 mask, and summing a mask
# is how this language counts - there is no count() and none is needed.
_ink = le(img, threshold)
Cells = rows(img) * cols(img)
Inked = sum(_ink)
Coverage = Cells > 0 ? Inked / Cells : 0
CoveragePct = Coverage * 100

# THE PICTURE'S OWN EXTENT, as a rectangle in metres - the outline drawn below. Built from the four
# placement readings rather than from the matrix, so it is exact rather than quantised to a cell.
# ONE LINE, deliberately: the parser matches `name = expr` per LINE, so a call broken across lines
# never parses and the name silently publishes 0.
_i = arange(4)
Extent = hcat(where(eq(_i,1) + eq(_i,2), originX + widthM, originX), where(eq(_i,2) + eq(_i,3), originY + heightM, originY))
WidthM = widthM
HeightM = heightM
AreaM2 = widthM * heightM
InkAreaM2 = AreaM2 * Coverage
CellM = cellM
